comparator.name: Art History (Kunstgeschiedenis)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 OER and current student curriculum define a 180-EC bachelor: a 120-EC major and 60-EC profiling space. The major contains two compulsory first-year basic packages (60 EC), two compulsory context courses (15 EC), one 30-EC depth package, and a 15-EC final paper. The target does not choose between the two formal depth packages, so the first package in the OER, Kunst en architectuur tot 1850, is instantiated by the official-order tie-break. The 60-EC profiling space is preserved without inventing a minor, exchange or internship.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized Kunstgeschiedenis target does not select between the two formal 30-EC depth packages. The adopted 2026–2027 OER lists Kunst en architectuur tot 1850 before Moderne en hedendaagse kunst en architectuur, so the former is selected by official order, before and independently of UCR course selection. The 60-EC profiling space remains open because the OER does not prescribe one subject.

core: Art history across periods, with analysis of painting, sculpture and architecture
Artistic materials, architectural form and the making of objects
Museums, collecting, display and cultural heritage
Visual analysis, art-historical methods, primary sources and historiography
Historical, cultural and social contexts of art
Advanced art-historical research and an independent final paper
adjacent: Art and architecture before 1850, including medieval, Renaissance and Golden Age material
Modern and contemporary art, architecture and visual culture in social context
questions: How do museums and heritage institutions select, display and interpret art?
How do artworks and visual media express cultural, historical and social ideas?
How do materials, techniques and built form shape the interpretation of art and architecture?

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

alternatives.label: Art History, Heritage & Visual Culture
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines eight art, archaeology and heritage courses with visual media, historical context and source-based research, providing the broadest feasible UCR response to Utrecht’s art-and-architecture major.
alternatives.concept: A balanced historical art and material-culture programme centred on UCR art history, archaeology, museums and heritage, with history, literature and visual media supplying context across periods and regions.
progression: All formal prerequisites and Fall-2026-cohort semester offerings were checked against the current enriched workbook. PPD is in the first semester. Introduction to Western Art History precedes later art-history courses; material culture, historical survey and media foundations generally precede advanced museum and research work. Seven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Art & Architecture before 1850
alternatives.labelReason: This route follows Utrecht’s formal pre-1850 depth package through Renaissance and ancient material culture, myth, heritage, and historical source work.
alternatives.concept: An early-art and architectural-history direction connecting Renaissance and ancient material culture to myth, historical context, heritage and primary-source interpretation.
progression: All formal prerequisites and Fall-2026-cohort offerings pass. PPD is in semester 1; introductory art history, archaeology, literature and history precede advanced heritage, interpretation and research. Seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad programme, four courses (30 EC) change in each direction: Perspectives on Literary Meaning, Histories of Gender, Western Way of War, and Life & Travel Writing replace introductory film/media, qualitative sociology, documentary, and Media & Race. The retained art-history core is reorganised around the formally documented pre-1850 direction.

alternatives.label: Modern & Contemporary Art, Media & Society
alternatives.labelReason: This route follows Utrecht’s formal modern and contemporary direction by combining modern art and museums with film, visual culture, public communication and social theory.
alternatives.concept: A modern and contemporary visual-culture programme linking art and museum study to film, communication, social theory and public debates about representation.
alternatives.distinctness: Eight courses (60 EC) differ in each direction from the broad programme, replacing historical, archaeological and literary contexts with television/social media, environment, communication and sociology. It also differs from the pre-1850 route by twelve courses (90 EC) in each direction.
progression: All formal prerequisites and Fall-2026-cohort offerings pass. PPD is in semester 1, and introductory art, media, communication and sociology courses precede advanced museum, representation and public-culture work. Seven 300-level courses are included.

candidates.label: Modern and contemporary art and architecture

selection.assessment: The broad art-history response owns the eight direct programme interests. Each of Utrecht’s two formal depth packages supplies an independently evidenced, coherent and mechanically feasible related direction. Their schedules differ from the broad programme by at least 30 EC and from each other by substantially more. Production stops because three UCR alternatives is the permitted maximum.

blocks: PPD provides broad academic development; Utrecht’s course is specifically an introduction to art-historical research.
Both introduce Western art history and visual interpretation; UCR begins with the Renaissance rather than antiquity.
Both analyse how cultural objects are made and interpreted through material evidence; UCR approaches this through archaeology.
UCR directly studies Renaissance painting, sculpture and architecture within Mediterranean exchange.
African Art & Heritage provides a substantive global and postcolonial art-history perspective with object research.
Both directly address modern and contemporary art; UCR emphasises museum display and interpretation.
Heritage & Ancient Democracy examines how material and architectural heritage is interpreted and used in the present.
Both examine art-historical methods, historiography, visual analysis and scholarly writing.
UCR offers ancient, Renaissance and modern material, but no selected course reproduces this dedicated late-antique and medieval survey.
No selected UCR course reproduces the comparator’s object-to-urban-scale architectural sequence.
UCR addresses architecture within art history and archaeology but lacks a dedicated pre-1850 architectural-history methods course.
UCR has no selected location-based Renaissance field course equivalent to the Florence excursion.
Global perspectives appear across UCR courses, but no single selected course reproduces this compulsory global-art context component.
World Myth & Literature studies the transfer of mythic narratives into images across cultures, supporting iconographic interpretation.
Both require sustained independent source-based research and argument; the UCR seminar is historical and smaller than the art-history thesis.
The genuine 60-EC profiling space is preserved without inventing a minor, exchange or internship.

notes.text: Utrecht provides a structured 120-EC art-history major with eight foundation courses, a formal four-course depth package, global and heritage context, and a 15-EC art-history final paper. UCR offers a smaller art-history and heritage sequence supported by archaeology, history, literature, media and cultural analysis; it does not reproduce the full specialist sequence, dedicated architectural-history progression or compulsory art-history thesis.
